parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is the island's own statute book: gender recognition since 2007, gender-identity employment protection since 2005, and a unanimous 2022 comprehensive anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, with no trans-specific criminalisation and no documented targeting, border friction, or violence. Parent-state equality law does not apply automatically, but that removes restrictions rather than adding them. Residual male homosexual private-life offences are a secondary, likely latent signal; prison placement for trans detainees is an open question, not a documented exposure. Travelling minors face no documented age-dependent rule. Structurally this sits just below the acceptance-with-working-protections tier, docked for the unresolved custody question and the archaic offence.

entry_documents.protection: No documented border screening targeting trans visitors; domestic gender-recognition since 2007 signals document-acceptant institutions.
entry_documents.interaction: No parent-state entry rules documented as extended to the island; border regime is the island's own.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: The single prison has no recorded rule on housing by birth sex vs gender identity, no trans unit, no segregation practice — placement unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Vulnerable-prisoner category exists; small facility (~99 held).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a visitor were detained, placement would be discretionary under an undocumented rule.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Parent single-sex services code (2025) not extended; island sets its own facilities practice with no documented restriction.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Island statute book governs facilities; parent law reaches only by order, none documented here.

care_services.protection: Comprehensive anti-discrimination law (effective Oct 2023) covers gender identity in services; gender recognition since 2007.
care_services.interaction: Visitor care access falls under island law; no refusal incidents documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Residual male homosexual offences for acts 'not in private' remain on the statute book — secondary, latent signal; no documented enforcement against trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Unanimous 2022 anti-discrimination bill rejecting all exemption amendments signals institutional non-hostility; no police targeting documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: No documented police lever against gender-nonconforming people.

minors_guardians.protection: Child-welfare anti-discrimination covering gender identity since 2008 (2016 on one island); no age-dependent visitor rule documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor encounters the same island-wide regime; no documented differentiation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence incidents documented with dates or outcomes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Working anti-discrimination enforcement framework from Oct 2023; socially reformist record (marriage vote, adoption rights) as climate signal.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin-data silence is not proof of safety, but structural signals point tolerant.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Prison placement practice and border treatment of trans travellers remain unsourced open questions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Comprehensive statute with no exemptions provides a remedy route; courts function within a rule-of-law parent tradition.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions weigh lightly; no documented exposure requiring remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A documents a universal, enforced visitor register and routine exclusion. This island documents no traveller-facing restriction at all; the comparison is far apart, with the island materially safer.

0.55-B has documented secondary screening and discretionary denial of trans visitors. Here no such friction is documented; only custody placement is an open question, placing the island above that tier.

0.85-A combines broad acceptance with documented enforcement actions (compensation, discipline). This island has comparable paper protections but thinner evidence of them operating, and an unresolved prison-placement rule — a step below, not a tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is the island's own: no trans-specific criminal offence, gender recognition since 2007, gender-identity employment protection since 2005, and a unanimous 2022 comprehensive anti-discrimination statute effective October 2023 — all documented positives under rule 3. Parent-state measures reach only by order, and none restricting visitors is documented as extended, so no external hostile layer applies. The residual male homosexual 'not in private' offence is a latent secondary signal, not an enforced lever against trans people. The worst feature is an open question — prison placement by birth sex vs identity — which holds the score below 0.85 but does not outweigh the absence of any documented traveller-facing exposure, targeting, or violence. A travelling minor faces the same regime with no documented age-dependent constraint.
